reasoning: Recent Kansas polling for the 2026 U.S. Senate race between Republican Sen. Roger Marshall and Democrat Adam Hamilton shows a very tight contest, with one August poll putting Marshall up 1 point and a July poll putting him up 4 points, implying an overall Republican edge of roughly R+2–3 in current data.[1][9] Major handicappers like Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball have recently shifted their Kansas Senate rating from Safe/Solid Republican to Likely Republican, reinforcing the view that while Kansas leans structurally Republican (about R+12 by Cook PVI), the current Senate race itself is competitive with only a small GOP advantage.[2][6][8][13] There is no new state-level presidential general-election polling in Kansas in the last 45 days from the required types of outlets, so the best quantified current margin we can state from recent data is for the Senate race: approximately R+2–3, based on the Marshall–Hamilton polls.

sources.name: The New York Times (reporting PPP/Senate Majority PAC poll)
sources.details: Public Policy Polling survey for Senate Majority PAC of the Kansas 2026 U.S. Senate general election found Roger Marshall leading Adam Hamilton 46%-45%, a 1-point Republican edge.

sources.name: The New York Times (reporting GBAO/Hamilton campaign poll)
sources.details: GBAO internal poll for the Hamilton campaign of the Kansas 2026 U.S. Senate general election showed Marshall leading Hamilton 47%-43%, a 4-point Republican edge.

sources.name: Daily Kos Elections (summarizing PPP and GBAO Kansas Senate polls)
sources.details: Daily Kos article summarizing two Kansas 2026 U.S. Senate general election polls reports a GBAO poll with Marshall +4 and a PPP/Senate Majority PAC poll with Marshall 46% to Hamilton 45%, describing the race as a dead heat overall.

sources.name: Kansas Reflector (reporting Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball ratings)
sources.details: Kansas Reflector article reports that Cook Political Report and Sabato’s Crystal Ball both shifted their rating of the 2026 Kansas U.S. Senate race from Safe/Solid Republican to Likely Republican, still favoring the GOP but acknowledging a more competitive environment.

sources.name: Sunflower State Journal (GBAO internal Democratic primary poll)
sources.details: Sunflower State Journal reports an internal Hamilton campaign primary poll by GBAO showing Adam Hamilton leading the Democratic primary field by 17 points among likely Kansas Democratic primary voters.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI Map and District List
sources.details: Cook Political Report’s PVI map lists Kansas as roughly R+12 at the statewide level, indicating a strong underlying Republican lean in its typical voting patterns compared to the nation as a whole.
sources.date_range: 2026 PVI release (state structural index, not a 2026 race poll)
